title: Finite-Temperature Transconductance of Multiterminal Josephson Junctions with Topological Andreev Spectra
authors: Gleb S. Seleznev, David C. Ohnmacht, Wolfgang Belzig
abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) provide a controllable platform for engineering topological Andreev spectra. At zero temperature, Andreev bound states (ABSs) with nonzero Chern numbers give rise to quantized transconductance between superconducting terminals. We derive the finite-temperature transconductance of MTJJs using linear-response theory. We first demonstrate the destructive role of temperature: changes in the thermal occupations of the ABSs destroy exact transconductance quantization. We then show that finite temperature can also play a constructive role by making the transconductance sensitive to finite-energy topological crossings hidden from the zero-temperature response. Our results establish the thermal limitations of transconductance quantization and identify finite-temperature transport as a probe of otherwise inaccessible topology in Andreev spectra.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes the transconductance of topological Josephson junctions at finite temperatures. It demonstrates that while temperature generally destroys perfect quantization, it can reveal subtle, individual topological features within the Andreev spectrum. This establishes finite-temperature transport as a powerful diagnostic tool for probing complex superconducting topology.
main_problem: The study investigates how finite temperature affects the quantized transconductance observed in multi-terminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) possessing topological Andreev spectra.
main_result: Temperature both destroys the exact quantization of transconductance and, constructively, allows the measurement of individual Andreev Bound State (ABS) topologies that are otherwise hidden at zero temperature.
method: The transconductance is derived using linear-response theory applied to the effective Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian describing the junction's ABSs.
model_or_system: The system is a multi-terminal Josephson junction (MTJJ) with $N$ superconducting leads, whose physics is governed by an effective BdG Hamiltonian. The analysis distinguishes between zero-energy and finite-energy topological crossings within the ABS spectrum.
key_observables: Transconductance ($G_{ij}$), ground-state Chern number ($C_{ij}$), individual-ABS Chern numbers ($C_{ij}^k$), and Berry curvature ($B_{ij}^k$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), superconducting phases ($\phi_\alpha$), and the junction geometry (number of terminals $N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes quasistatic thermal equilibrium and utilizes linear-response theory, neglecting continuum states.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the four-terminal MTJJ setup, the ABS spectra versus phase, and the mechanism of topological crossings (both zero-energy and finite-energy).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the $T=0$ quantization based on the ground-state Chern number, then extends the analysis to finite temperature using linear-response theory to show both the destructive and constructive roles of thermal excitations.
why_interesting: The work connects topological invariants (Chern numbers) to measurable transport quantities (transconductance) under non-zero temperature conditions, providing a thermal probe for otherwise inaccessible quantum properties.

(a) At the zero- energy WP ϕ3 = ϕZE, the negative- and positive-energy branches change their Chern numbers by −QZE and +QZE, giving ∆C12 = −QZE. (b) Particle-hole-related finite- energy WPs occur at E = ±ϵFE and ϕ3 = ϕFE. At each crossing, the lower and upper branches change their Chern numbers by −QFE and +QFE, while the ground-state Chern number remains unchanged, ∆C12 = 0.

Both double-QD models contain normal hopping rN; the shared leads 1 and 2 in panel (c) additionally generate the nonlocal SC coupling rSC. Neighboring SC leads in panel (a) are directly coupled by t.
